idiom_name: ktlint standard rules (four-space indent) plus require/check guard conditions
implementation_notes: Kotlin's official coding conventions fix the shape - four spaces per level, no tabs, braces on the same line as the declaration - and ktlint applies them with no configuration required, its indent rule driven by .editorconfig, which gives the same 'run the tool, get the rectangle' story as gofmt even though ktlint is not part of the compiler distribution. What replaces the classic structure: require and check express preconditions as guard clauses that throw, early returns shorten the normal path, and expression-bodied functions remove a brace level entirely. The classic multi-line brace form remains right for anything with more than a couple of statements.
pitfalls: Expression bodies and trailing lambdas tempt one-liners that nest several closures inside a single line; indentation rules cannot rescue a line that hides three levels.
Multi-line when-entries are re-indented by ktlint's rules, so hand-aligning arrows produces output that changes on every format run.
Editors default to IntelliJ's continuation indent (8) while ktlint's official style uses none; mismatched settings make a file unformattable without a large diff.
